verdict.line: You lose if you grind extended trades where his passive and E sustain him through it; you win if you close the kill fast with E and W before he stabilizes.

brief.thesis: Kled gets first-strike advantage because Skaarl's extra health pool and the Jousting (E) + Violent Tendencies (W) burst combo threaten a kill before Aatrox has leveled his Q stacks or built up Deathbringer Stance sustain. But Aatrox's kit is built to punish the follow-through: his Q (The Darkin Blade) can interrupt your E return dash if you path back through him, and his passive plus Umbral Dash (E) healing let him win fights that go long. That's why the raw head-to-head sits at 48.3% over 143 games, slightly under Kled's 49.7% baseline, even though the lane and solo-kill stats favor you — the advantage is real but only if you cash it in early.

theirWindow.when: when his Q and W are both ready
theirWindow.what: Do not commit to an extended trade or chase with your E return dash through him — his Q can interrupt that second Jousting hit, and his W (Infernal Chains, 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown) drags you back into it if you linger in the impact zone.

yourWindow.when: when Aatrox's Q and W are both down
yourWindow.what: All-in immediately: Jousting (E) in, pop Violent Tendencies (W) for the four-attack burst, and commit to the kill. This is when his interrupt and his engage tool are both gone, so your solo-kill advantage actually lands.

boots.why: 80.3% pick at 44.1% winrate — Aatrox's whole kit is physical autos and sword slams, so flat armor blunts both his trades and his Deathbringer Stance procs.

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's stacking adaptive force rewards exactly the extended skirmishes your W burst sets up, and the healing on takedown helps offset Aatrox's own sustain if the fight runs long.

summoners.why: 84.3% pick rate at 48.7% winrate — Ignite denies Aatrox's Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash healing during your all-in window, which is the difference between a trade and the solo kill you're favored for.

playing.title: Force fights before level 6
playing.detail: Your W+E burst combo threatens a kill while Aatrox still lacks full Q stacks and World Ender; this is your highest-leverage window before the matchup evens out.

playing.title: Never chase through him with E
playing.detail: The second half of Jousting dashes back through your original target — if that path crosses Aatrox while his Q is up, he interrupts it. Bait his Q first or don't return through him.

playing.title: Punish Infernal Chains whiffs hard
playing.detail: His W is on a 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown — if it misses, he has no engage tool for a long window. That's when your solo-kill advantage is safest to execute.

playing.title: Track your own dismount state
playing.detail: Once Skaarl's health depletes, your Q swaps from a hook to Pocket Pistol and you deal less to champions — plan trades around staying mounted, not around winning while dismounted.

playing.title: Build Grievous Wounds if sustain stalls you
playing.detail: If Deathbringer Stance procs and Umbral Dash healing are keeping Aatrox topped off through your trades, prioritize Executioner's Calling or Mortal Reminder to cut that back.

playing.title: Close the lane, don't grind it
playing.detail: The 48.3% head-to-head sits below your 49.7% baseline despite your stated lane and solo-kill edge — that gap is Aatrox's late-trade sustain clawing it back, so end the lane early rather than let it go long.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample figures above are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning — why the Q-interrupt matters, when to all-in, how dismounting changes your trades — is my own tactical read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Always be wary of Aatrox’s abilities’ range. His The Darkin Blade (Q) can interrupt Jousting [E] so try to keep your distance while contesting lane.
